content: The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) website provides detailed recommendations regarding the disinsection of aircraft. These recommendations align with the guidelines issued by the World Health Organization (WHO) as outlined in the WHO Weekly Epidemiological Record from 1985 and 1987, including specific issues such as No. 7 (1985, p. 47), No. 12 (1985, p. 90), No. 45 (1985, pp. 345-346), and No. 44 (1987, pp. 335-336), along with any subsequent amendments. Aircraft disinsection treatments must be renewed if cleaning or other operations remove a significant amount of the residual disinsection product. Annex 9 of the ICAO guidelines, titled Facilitation, specifies that any individual displaying symptoms such as appearing visibly unwell, persistent coughing, difficulty breathing, ongoing diarrhea, persistent vomiting, skin rashes, unexplained bruising or bleeding, or sudden confusion may be suspected of having a communicable disease. This also applies to cases of illness disembarked during a previous stop. Details of all disinsection or sanitary treatments conducted during a flight, including the location, date, time, and method, must be documented. The General Declaration form, which is for official use only, must be completed with precise and truthful information to the best of the declarant's knowledge. This includes supplementary forms, if required, and confirmation that all passengers have continued or will continue on the flight. The document must be signed by an authorized agent or the pilot-in-command. The size of the document is standardized to 210 mm × 297 mm (8 ¼ × 11 ¾ inches). Certain sections of the form are to be completed only when required by the State, and passenger manifests may replace some sections if presented. These guidelines are sourced from the International Civil Aviation Organization.
